body:
from the latest technical strategy discussion with Drew, Rich, Ramsey, and Thom - think we are going to move forward with an EDG-to-ETH bridge (possibly via Polygon) once ERUP4 is live.

Unless there are any more volunteers I'll be the node runner and relayer for that. It's all deployed in public and auditable, so there should not be any risk to assets.

[@Alan](/edgeware/account/o3SYRfwKAS9zs1b5hrji73EUgVBpzK3XRg9A2FiErMR3rks) EDG can be custodied in the bridge and minted on ETH, but ETH assets can't be custodied and minted on EDG, which would reduce the risk posed by people bridging over a large amount of, say, USDC for example.

[@raymondz](/edgeware/account/mae7JWE1EEMLcno2ZSB8dahwPqVPEyh8zik6dgNpQTvvucq) that's an interesting idea, that claims pallet is quite useful. I'm guessing Edgeware havent used it yet because they didnt fundraise in the typical way. But Polkadot used it so people claim their DOT from ETH, and also their KSM (i believe).

Interesting thoughts, definitely helping to develop my simple nebulous thought. 

My questions are whats is the optimal amount of EDG to make available on Uniswap? Is there an optimal range with min and max or does just an arbitrary number suffice?

6 months for Uniswap holders to claim is also an arbitrary number,, ,perhaps it can be shorter. A "claims.json" would need to be updated that maps ERC20 addresses to EDG addresses.

Whatever devs are excited about is the approach we should go ahead with..no problem holding back chainbridge / making another attempt at setting up the bridge post-parachain bonding.

If that means holding some EDG  in a smart contract that's a very straightforward plan and easy to execute.

To expand slightly on my comment, following on from a quick discussion with Ramsey, offline.  What I was trying to suggest was starting with a smart contract holding EDG (wEDG?) backed by a promise / IOU, and then upgrade that same smart contract to a swap and burn smart contract mirrored by a similar SC on the Edgeware side - so that the initial smart contract address on the Ethereum side would remain valid when the swap and burn capability is added.

I've no idea if it's viable or what it would require in the way of bridging.  I'm not even sure it's especially novel.  Just an idea to bounce around and see it if adds value.

This is cool, and a thoughtful step towards full bridging between EDG and ETH - would certainly support it.

Another option could be a unidirectional bridge of EDG to ETH.

I know a little more about this having set up and tested a USDC-to-Beresheet trusted bridge last week...

The benefit of that is that if we hard spoon EDG onto DOT and have to migrate the bridge, we have an easy failsafe to get bridged EDG holders their mainnet EDG (as Ramsey described, it would require a snapshot and using the claims pallet).

Is that something we should consider too?

[@JelliedOwl (Paul)](/edgeware/account/5GEfWPdRcHyveFUcRWAqy1hNWnBsywtWgce5kmdN4scw8VXz) I dont think you necessarily need to swap for EDG to cash out. You can just sell your EDG20 on Uniswap?

I put 6 months just because you need to update the claims pallet with a JSON file of all the ERC20 contract addresses, so i imagine that should happen in intervals. 6 months is just an arbitrary number. 

Sorry if i missed what you meant.

Is there's a viable way to write the token contract so that the ERC-20 token starts "naked" but can be backfilled (and possibly added to as a defato "wEDG on ETH" token when the development catches up?  So there wouldn't be a need to explicit swap back to cash out - and maybe the 6 months would be just to cover the "we expected to have this bridge by now but there's are tech issues still - so you can cash out back to EDG on Edgeware if you want" scenario?  (If any of that makes sense.)

Ideally becoming true wEDG without needing to change the contact address on the Eth side...
